references.text: Israel settled in all the cities of the Amorites, including Heshbon, which was Sihon's capital. This provides the historical background for why the tribe of Reuben could build up Heshbon.
Heshbon and Elealeh are mentioned among the cities in the fertile land east of the Jordan that the tribes of Reuben and Gad asked to receive as their inheritance.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord gave them victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, which led to their taking possession of this area.
Heshbon and its plains are mentioned as part of the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben when the land was divided under Joshua.
Heshbon was given to the Levites from the tribe of Reuben as a Levitical city with pastureland.
Isaiah prophesies about Heshbon and Elealeh in connection with judgment against Moab, showing these cities' continued significance.
Heshbon and Elealeh are mentioned together again in Isaiah's prophecy concerning Moab.
Jeremiah mentions Heshbon and Elealeh in his prophecy against Moab, where the cry is heard from these cities.
Heshbon is mentioned as Sihon's city in Jeremiah's judgment against Moab.
